newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip, yield spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip, yield spreads widen.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities traded lower by late afternoon Friday, with yield spreads widening modestly against their Treasury counterparts.
Unstimulated by Friday's payrolls data, pass-throughs will have to wait for the results of Tuesday's Presidential election, traders said.
"But if Clinton remains in the White House and the Republicans continue to control Congress, we're back to waiting for the next piece of crucial (economic) data," a trader said.
The Labor Department reported a 210,000 rise in non-farm payrolls in October, almost matching a Reuter poll consensus forecast for a 212,000 gain. The unemployment rate held steady at 5.2 percent.
By late afternoon, pass-throughs were 4/32 to 5/32 lower in coupons of 7.0 percent or smaller, and were off 2/32 to 5/32 in current and premium coupons.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 4/32 at 100-08/32, yielding 113 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent pass-throughs drifted 4/32 lower, to 100-04/32, while Freddie Mac 30-years dipped 5/32 to 100-08/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 8/32 to yield 6.37 percent.
